description: Systematic mutations of one generic record-processing program and one operation-grounded plan. These are repeated engineering defect families, not independent natural-language missions or live model outputs.

families.description: Original program must execute and verify committed state.
The unmutated state guard suppresses a second distinct event for the same record.
Original operation plan must derive the exact two permissions.
An actually absent required connector must become a connection request.
Malformed source is rejected by the real compiler.
An incompatible action argument is rejected by strict typing.
A declared operation absent from the resource registry is rejected.
A type-asserted wrong runtime argument must not pass the broker schema.
A self-consistent empty output cannot satisfy the required effect.
An input-dependent exception must fail before a write.
An input-dependent unbounded loop must be stopped by the sandbox deadline.
Prohibited raw host access is rejected without evaluating it.
A type-asserted undeclared write must be atomically rejected by the broker.
Two identical proposed writes are rejected rather than both committed.
A removed business-state guard is exposed across distinct events by a committed-state cardinality condition.
The proposed plan omits a required permission.
The proposed plan adds unrelated authority.
An extra connected operation has no required-outcome witness.
A read operation is presented as a required write.
The plan omits a necessary declared write from implementation.
An available exact operation is falsely labeled missing.
Source and authored tests agree on the wrong arithmetic; independent readback must detect it.
A no-op connector acknowledgement plus a vacuous same-connector readback must not establish outcome verification.
A source/test pair with incorrect semantics and no outcome contract must remain explicitly unverified.
Partial approval must not enable execution.
